p.s: I think that specializing in one subject is better than having a broad knowledge of many academics subjects, and this for many reasons.
At the time you begin studies where you have the choice to specialize or not, which means you 're entering University you already had a large view of different topics during high school years.
So a majority of people already know what tehy like and was is theiy are good at Specializing is also a good way to quickly do what you think you are made for.
It also allows people to find a job quicker as they have been specialising earlier.
During high school years pupils study a large variety of subjects and most of tehm at the end know what they like.
It can be rather science, litterature, sport, economy.
Thus they can already know where their point of interest are and specialize already in their freshman year.
It is time and money consuming to study subjects that you are not really interested in and that wo n't be useful in you career or even in your personal development.

If you think you like for example physics, studying it at the beginning of your university years will enable you, first to see if you really want to be a physician, second to have a greater involvement in what you are studying, by following more class and conducing more experiments.
An other important point is that by being more specialize it is more easy to find a job at the end of your studies.
People think specialist are more reliable in the task they are given to do than others.
However somes could say that by specializing you miss the big picture of the broad knowledge offered at Univerisity.
They also think that specialist are boringing people only focused on their subject.
It 's oftenly not true, if you specialize in one subject during courses you can also have many other center of interests outside your College our University.
You can be studying sciences like maths and play soccer at a very high level.
Some rugbymen who played in the English national were in fact doctors.
You can also focus on poetry and be interested in economy and learn it not as an academic subject.
Thus, I think that spezialing in one subject is not only the most efficient way of studying it'also a way to accomplish yourself through something you realy like and are able to do.
